Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a lightweight checklist and attached examples.

1) Checksums: we accept SHA-256 (preferred) and SHA-1 for legacy artifacts. Please include the algorithm name as a column in the manifest.
2) Signed manifests: recommended but not mandatory. If you can provide a manifest signed with your org's GPG or a signed object with a metadata signature field, we will mark it as high-confidence provenance. Mandatory manifest fields: bundle_id, file_path, file_size_bytes, checksum_value, checksum_algo, uploaded_by, upload_ts.
3) Delta rules: we allow up to 2 filename normalization adjustments (character-encoding, leading/trailing whitespace) per bundle. Any missing file listed in the manifest causes a rejection. Renames must be reflected in the manifest; an uploaded file whose checksum matches an entry will be accepted even if the filename is slightly different, provided you include original_filename in the manifest notes.

Delegated uploader checklist (high level):
- Confirm bundle_id namespace (nbridge-YYYYMMDD-##)
- Run checksum (SHA-256) on each file, add to manifest as checksum_value and checksum_algo
- Validate manifest schema (attached CSV template)
- Place bundle in staging S3 path: s3://nbridge-whistic-staging/<bundle_id>/
- Trigger Whistic ingestion job and paste ingestion ticket URL in the manifest notes
- Keep a signed copy of manifest (GPG or KMS-signed) for 90 days for audit

I've attached: evidence_manifest_v3.csv (CSV template), sample_checksum.txt (example SHA-256 output), and a short delegated_uploader_checklist.pdf.

If you want, Marissa can add this wording into our SOC 2 evidence appendix so the language is consistent across the runbook.

Best,
